clue.text: Do away with heartless order after period

indicators.note: the order word is placed after the period word

parts.note: an era is a period of history

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word for order is cut out

parts.note: to dictate is to order or command

explanation.surface: An instruction to abolish an order, issued once a certain period has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' means the middle letter of the order word goes; 'after' puts that trimmed word behind the period.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with something is to wipe it out completely, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Brought up as left-winger absorbing Listener

indicators.note: the left-winger takes in the listener, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone raised as a socialist who has taken in a radio audience, or a Listener magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Listener' suggests the old BBC magazine, but it is simply the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who are brought up are raised or nurtured, a direct synonym.

clue.text: It could be due to introduction of roadworks

definitions.text: It could be due to introduction of roadworks

indicators.note: the letters of the two words may become something else when rearranged
the opening letter of the word roadworks is taken

explanation.surface: A remark about what might result from roadworks starting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DUE TO into DETOU; 'introduction of' adds R, the first letter of roadworks. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadworks often force traffic onto a diversion, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Yarn from northern town, last bit from mill

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, in the north-west of England

indicators.note: the final letter of the word mill is taken

explanation.surface: Wool spun in a northern English mill town.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a town in Cheshire, England; L is the final letter of mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool used for embroidery, a specific kind of thread.

clue.text: Material from message landing on French island

indicators.note: in a down answer the message piece sits on top of the island piece

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: Fabric brought in by a message delivered to an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: A textile is a woven fabric or cloth, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: A scent drifts around our mistress

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the word our
the letters of the two words drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A perfume wafting about the woman who is our lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifts' rearranges A SCENT into CTESAN; 'around' puts that round OUR, after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a kept woman of a wealthy patron, a historical kind of mistress.

clue.text: Disorder with one opposing speech, wanting Conservative out

parts.note: a con is an argument or person against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: wanting here means lacking, so the letter goes missing from the speech word
taken out from the speech word, completing the removal instruction

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A disordered political debate in which the Conservative speaker has been ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like part of the surface's chaos but is the definition, in its medical sense; 'wanting ... out' removes the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition is a medical complaint or ailment, the same sense as a disorder.

clue.text: Justified having got angry after conflict

indicators.note: the angry word follows the conflict word

parts.note: war is armed conflict
to rant is to speak angrily

explanation.surface: Someone excused for losing their temper once the fighting started.
explanation.definitionFit: Warranted means deserved or justified, as in a warranted complaint.

clue.text: Little woman and patient man meeting by a shrub

parts.note: Jo March is one of the heroines of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
Job is the Biblical figure famed for his patience

explanation.surface: A small woman and a long-suffering man meet beside a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Jojoba is a desert evergreen bush whose seeds yield a cosmetic oil.

clue.text: Ferocious woman that could cut one dead

definitions.meaning: a weapon for war that could kill someone, playing on cut dead meaning to snub

explanation.surface: A fierce woman who might snub you, or worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a formidable, bossy woman and literally names a heavy medieval weapon.

clue.text: Dealer looking embarrassed with paintings being returned?

indicators.note: the two words together are read backwards, as if sent back

parts.note: an embarrassed face turns red
art is paintings collectively

explanation.surface: An art dealer blushing as his paintings are sent back to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who buys and sells, which is what any dealer does.

clue.text: Unco-operative type? Right — I seek fun, somehow

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: A self-centred person declaring they are only after a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I SEEK FUN into EFUSENIK, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusenik was a Soviet Jew denied emigration; now anyone who refuses to comply, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Comedian appearing in Cromer tonight

indicators.note: the letters appear inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: A comic billed to perform at the Norfolk seaside resort of Cromer this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromer is a seaside town in Norfolk; the name runs across cro(MER TON)ight.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Merton is a British comic known for panel shows such as Have I Got News for You.

clue.text: Tired friend in a no-win situation

parts.note: stale means tired or jaded
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A weary companion stuck in a situation with no winner.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a stalemate ends the game with neither side winning; figuratively any deadlock.

clue.text: Clever character finds way to avoid using cash

parts.note: smart means clever
a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: A shrewd person discovers a method of paying without money.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartcard has an embedded chip used for payment, letting one pay electronically instead of with notes.

clue.text: Spot American going after brave man, a famous Greek

indicators.note: the spot and American pieces follow the brave man piece

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: An American spotted trailing a hero who turns out to be a celebrated Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus, called the father of history, was an ancient historian from Halicarnassus.

clue.text: Stone gleams — just the odd bits of it

indicators.text: just the odd bits of it
indicators.note: only the first, third and fifth letters of the word gleams are kept

explanation.surface: A precious stone shines, if only in patches.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem is a precious stone such as a ruby or diamond.

clue.text: A son of Jacob? Gosh!

definitions.meaning: One of the twelve sons of Jacob in Genesis, founder of a tribe of Israel
an old mild oath, a euphemism for God

explanation.definitionFit: Gad is both a Biblical son of Jacob and a dated exclamation of surprise like 'by gad'.

clue.text: Time of year for one with aspirations to lead party?

definitions.text: one with aspirations to lead party?
definitions.meaning: Theresa ..., who sought and won the Conservative leadership in 2016

explanation.surface: Asking at what season an ambitious politician makes a bid for leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a calendar month and that of the British Prime Minister who led the Conservatives.

clue.text: Moderate a sort of emulsion for painting

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or soften

explanation.surface: An instruction to tone down a kind of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint medium made by binding pigment in egg yolk, an emulsion used by early artists.

clue.text: A hit poem in the modern style

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A hit poem written in up-to-date fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means fashionable or in the current style.

clue.text: Unemotional doctor dealt with last character in surgery

indicators.note: the final letter of the word surgery is taken

explanation.surface: A detached GP who saw the final patient at the clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry describes a manner that is matter-of-fact and lacking warmth or feeling.

clue.text: Plant, one on slope above

indicators.note: in a down answer the slope piece sits above the others

parts.note: a ramp is a slope
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plant growing on the hillside overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampion is a bellflower whose roots and leaves were once eaten in salads.

clue.text: Piece of bacon Ronald grilled

indicators.note: the name is cooked so that its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ronald cooking a rasher under the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardon is a small strip or cube of fatty bacon used in cooking.

clue.text: European leader offering his neighbouring country almost nothing

indicators.note: the country's name loses its last letter

parts.note: France borders Spain
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A European ruler offering the country next door practically nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FRANCE to FRANC; 'his' refers to the definition's leader, Spain's General Franco.
explanation.definitionFit: General Franco was dictator of Spain from 1939 until 1975.

clue.text: Merry bishop not at all like Friar Tuck

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

parts.words: not at all like Friar Tuck
parts.note: Friar Tuck of the Robin Hood stories is portly, so the opposite is lithe, supple and slim

explanation.surface: A jolly churchman who is nothing like the stout friar of Robin Hood's band.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree, a synonym of merry.

clue.text: Author participating in Eastern expedition

indicators.note: the letters take part in the two words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A writer joining a journey to the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across ea(STERN E)xpedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy and A Sentimental Journey.

clue.text: Lack of certain standards in test getting in the way of friendly relations

indicators.note: the test piece obstructs, sitting inside the friendship word

parts.note: amity is friendship or friendly relations
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An exam interfering with a friendship, leading to moral lapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in the way of' means the test word interrupts the friendship word, sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorality is the absence of any moral principles at all.

clue.text: Mark's mother, short ugly woman

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: Mark's mum described as a squat, unattractive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a man's name but is the definition. 'short' trims CRONE to CRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A macron is the bar placed over a vowel to show it is long, a diacritical sign.

clue.text: High-up person's little good, fool appearing in newspaper column

indicators.note: the good and fool pieces show up inside the column word

parts.note: a diary is a gossip column in a newspaper
G is the short form of good
a nit is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.surface: A grandee whose small kindness and foolishness get reported in the gossip pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary is a person of high rank or office, someone eminent.

clue.text: Arrive feeling elated after dizzy spell?

indicators.note: the elated piece follows the dizzy spell piece

parts.note: a turn is a brief attack of illness or giddiness
up means in high spirits

explanation.surface: Someone arriving in high spirits after a funny turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is the everyday phrase for arriving or appearing.

clue.text: Exposed, as cold maiden maybe in nude shivering

indicators.note: the cold and maiden pieces go inside the shuffled letters
the letters of the word nude tremble into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, one example of an over

explanation.surface: A naked person shivering, laid bare like a maiden in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a maiden is an over without runs. 'shivering' rearranges NUDE into UNED, and 'in' puts COVER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncovered means laid bare or revealed, a synonym of exposed.
